discussion_comments.comment_body:
**MAJOR (latent):** `appendToListField`'s regex `^(${field}:\n(?:  - .+\n)*)` only matches block-form lists, so it silently returns the content unchanged for the inline empty form - and three core initialization stages ship exactly that:

```
core/aidlc-common/stages/initialization/state-init.md:9:            produces: []
core/aidlc-common/stages/initialization/workspace-detection.md:9:   produces: []
core/aidlc-common/stages/initialization/workspace-scaffold.md:9:    produces: []
```

(same for `sensors: []`). `appendConsumes` handles `consumes: []` explicitly (the emptyRe branch), so the asymmetry looks unintentional. Today's test-pro contributions all target block-form stages, so this is latent - but any future plugin contributing produces/sensors to those stages loses the adds with no error or log.

Suggested fix: mirror the `consumes: []` handling for produces/sensors (replace `field: []` with a block), and log a warning when a contribution's adds cannot be applied instead of returning silently.

Fixed in `fb50f0d`. `mergeListField()` now handles the inline-empty `field: []` form explicitly (replacing it with a block) in addition to the block form, so a contribution targeting a stage that ships `produces: []` no longer silently drops. `mergeConsumes()` handles `consumes: []` the same way.

**[MAJOR] The documented contribution contract is wider than these three merges, and the gap is silent.**

- doc 18 section 5 lists produces/consumes/sensors/required_sections/scopes as set-union surfaces (plus `adds.requires_stage` in the table); compose implements exactly three. Unhandled `adds.*` keys fall through with no recordDrop, contrary to this file's own no-silent-failures contract. The shipped fixture itself declares `adds.required_sections` in all four contribution files; all of them vanish at compose.
- `plugin.json`'s `aidlc.contributes` block is read by nothing (compose.ts and package.ts hardcode the directory sets), and doc 18 line 82's "strict (unknown keys rejected)" has no implementing code
- section 3's `agents/`, `scopes/`, `memory/`, `knowledge/` subtrees never reach dist (package.ts `contentDirs` excludes them)
- the `when:` predicate is schema-validated and documented as live semantics (18:168; 10-authoring:107) but has zero engine consumers (aidlc-graph.ts:948 names itself the future home), so `test-pro-full-suite` is unconditionally EXECUTE under its scope

Either implement the missing surfaces, or recordDrop unhandled keys and demote the doc passages to future tense. Right now an author following the doc gets silent no-ops.

Addressed in `7c00c7f`. `required_sections` is now an implemented merge surface (it adds the field to a target that lacks it — verified on build-and-test, which ships none). Any unhandled `adds.*` key is now recorded to the drops log (no silent no-op). The genuinely-deferred surfaces are demoted to future tense in doc 18 §3/§5/§6 with an explicit §8 Status list: `adds.scopes`/`adds.requires_stage` (declared → logged, not merged), plugin `agents/`/`scopes/`/`memory/`/`knowledge/` projection, `when:` evaluation (parsed, no engine consumer), and `aidlc.contributes`/lockfile reading. So an author following the doc no longer gets a silent no-op — either it merges or it's logged + documented as deferred.

**[MAJOR, blocking] Compose writes a frontmatter key an older installed engine rejects, permanently breaking that install's graph compile.**

mergeRequiredSections edits the core stage file in place. On an install whose engine predates this PR (any released 2.2.x dist tree), `required_sections` is not in the schema's OPTIONAL_FIELDS and unknown keys are rejected, so after one compose every subsequent graph compile on that install fails with `unknown key: required_sections`. There is no backup, uninstalling the plugin does not revert the stage file, and the only trace is a .drops line, so it presents as workflow routing being silently stale forever.

This is the default adoption path once the plugin is installable from a store: old engine + new plugin is the normal state of the world after any release (the upgrade instruction is "re-copy your dist shell", which users skip). The seam for the fix already exists: the hook dynamic-imports the installed lib for hooksHealthDir. Probing the installed schema the same way (or dry-running validateStageFrontmatter on the merged frontmatter and rolling back plus drop-logging on rejection) makes compose safe against version skew in both directions.

Fixed in `54faa29`. compose now probes the INSTALLED engine before writing `required_sections`: `installedSchemaAccepts("required_sections", …)` runs the installed `validateStageFrontmatter` against a minimal valid stage carrying the key, once per run. If the installed schema rejects it (older dist), the merge is skipped and drop-logged ("installed engine does not accept 'required_sections' … re-copy your dist shell") instead of written. Verified both directions: current engine merges it; a simulated pre-PR engine (schema with required_sections stripped) skips it AND the install still compiles cleanly — no permanent unknown-key break. Reused the existing hooksHealthDir dynamic-import seam.

**[MINOR, non-blocking - follow-up PR is fine] The compile self-heal keys on stage slugs, so contributions-only plugins still never retry.**

`if (pluginSlugs.length === 0) return false` means a transient compile failure after a contribution merge is recorded once (visible in doctor now, thanks) but never retried: the stage source carries the merge, the compiled graph does not, and nothing recompiles until some unrelated change flips `changed`. For a stage-carrying plugin the heal works (verified: stripped the slugs from a composed graph, reran, 34 stages restored), so this is just the zero-stage case. Recompiling whenever the previous run recorded a compile drop would close it; a t188 case that strips the graph and asserts the heal would pin the behavior, which is currently the one claimed fix with no test.

Fixed in `54faa29`. The self-heal no longer keys only on stage slugs: a project-side retry marker (`aidlc/.plugin-compose-retry-<plugin>`) is written on compile failure and cleared on success, so a contributions-only plugin retries next run too. Added a t188 case that strips the plugin stages from the compiled graph and asserts the rerun restores them (the one claimed fix that lacked a test — now pinned, 12/12).

This pushes `pass:false` for any present marker, and a `pass:false` result flips doctor to exit 1 (line 1747). But a FRESH marker is the normal state at a live compose gate (written before the gate, deleted on resolve), so `/aidlc --doctor` run while a gate is legitimately open — a second terminal, or CI — reports a red row and non-zero exit on a healthy workspace. The `, fresh`/`, stale` label is already computed two lines up but ignored for `pass`. Suggest: `pass: ageMs <= COMPOSE_MARKER_TTL_MS` (fresh = advisory pass, only stale fails), matching how the other 'not a fault' rows (rule drift, leaked locks) are modeled as `pass:true`.
